title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff and regional failover ordering to avoid load-shedding thrash
author: Taylor Nguyen
description: Hotfix to address a production incident where the SLO enforcer entered a backoff thrash loop during partial regional failover. Symptoms: rapid open/close of circuit-breakers, aggressive load-shedding on stable regions, and client-facing 503s during multi-region routing events. Root cause: backoff timers were being reset by out-of-order region state updates and a missing quorum check for enforcer decisions; hysteresis wasn't applied consistently across the regional failover path. This change: 1) introduces an ordering guard for region-state transitions to ensure failover decisions are applied deterministically, 2) adds a quorum-based decision step before escalating to global load-shedding (requires majority of region enforcers to agree), 3) refactors backoff/hysteresis state machine so resets require an explicit recovery signal (instead of any successful probe), and 4) tightens thresholds for emergency load-shedding while adding a short, capped randomized jitter to reduce synchronized thundering. Also adds: telemetry (slo.enforcer.decision_reason, slo.enforcer.quorum, slo.enforcer.hysteresis_state), an e2e integration test that simulates staggered region outages, and a stress test that replicates the production request patterns we saw during the incident. Rollout plan: deploy to Dedicated-canary (small subset of customers) for 1 hour, monitor slo.enforcer.* metrics and error budget burn, then rollout to Hosted production with 10% canary -> 50% -> 100%. Backout: revert to previous enforcer config and disable regional failover routing policy. See linked linear tickets for investigation and postmortem. This description includes the rationale, quick mitigation guidance, and tests to prevent recurrence.
